name: Rancid
label: Epitaph
lede: Two Albany kids from Operation Ivy, a Madonna offer they turned down, and a hit album that put the East Bay on MTV.

eras.title: Out of the ashes of Operation Ivy
eras.text: Two Albany kids who had played together since Little League watched their first band explode at Gilman Street. One of them was drinking himself homeless. Rancid was the way back.

years.h: [[Operation Ivy|931e1d1f-6b2f-4ff8-9f70-aa537210cd46]] play their last show at 924 Gilman Street
years.p: [[Tim Armstrong|beaecc2d-20c7-4221-8fd2-682c82f0faab]] and [[Matt Freeman|dfb5e502-25a3-4ccc-94be-45da1642f689]] end the Berkeley ska-punk band the night their only album is coming out. It becomes a cult record later.
years.xp:
Operation Ivy formed in 1987 around the all-ages co-op at 924 Gilman Street, with Armstrong on guitar, Freeman on bass, Jesse Michaels on vocals and Dave Mello on drums. Freeman later told Larry Livermore the band "wasn't that fun anymore".

Armstrong's Wikipedia biography says he battled depression and alcoholism afterward and became homeless.

years.cap: Nova Rock 2017 Matt Freeman from Rancid at the Nova Rock 2017 · Wikimedia
q: I never thought about being famous or putting out a record.
years.h: Rancid starts: Tim, Matt and roommate Brett Reed
years.p: Freeman pushed Armstrong to start a new band. Armstrong got sober, wrote songs, and Brett Reed took the drum seat.
years.xp:
According to Armstrong's Wikipedia biography, Freeman suggested a new band partly to help Armstrong with his addiction. Armstrong started writing in 1991 and the trio played parties and Gilman shows.

Armstrong told Larry Livermore's interview: "I never thought about being famous or putting out a record."

eras.title: From Lookout to Epitaph
eras.text: A first EP on Lookout, a short stay in a small punk scene's biggest tent, then a move to Brett Gurewitz's label. The trio recorded a debut and picked up a second guitarist.

years.h: First EP on Lookout! Records
years.p: Rancid's first record comes out on the Berkeley label before they sign to Epitaph.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the band's first release to 1992 on Lookout!, the Berkeley label run by Larry Livermore, home to Operation Ivy and Green Day. Rancid moved to [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]]'s Epitaph shortly after.

years.h: Rancid: the trio debut, made in Culver City
years.p: Fifteen fast songs cut at Westbeach Recorders with producer Donnell Cameron. Brett Gurewitz sang backup.
years.xp: Recorded from September 1992 to January 1993, the debut has no ska at all, AllMusic noted, just heavy bass leads and Armstrong's slurred vocals. It was the first of three Rancid albums with the same title.

q: This is what I've been waiting for my whole life.
years.h: [[Lars Frederiksen|be04e717-683a-46de-a302-33d8ddb47884]] auditions and joins as second guitarist
years.p: A 19-year-old Operation Ivy fan from the South Bay, formerly with the UK Subs on their 1991 tour, becomes the band's second guitarist.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Lars debuted on the 1993 EP Radio Radio Radio. He was later credited on the supporting tour of the debut but declined credit on the album itself, so as not to take credit for it.

In Livermore's interview he described hearing the band: "This is what I've been waiting for my whole life."

eras.title: The punk boom and the Madonna offer
eras.text: After Green Day and the Offspring broke, major labels came calling. Rancid said no, made their biggest record, and got on MTV anyway.

years.h: Let's Go: 23 songs in six days
years.p: Brett Gurewitz produces at Fantasy Studios in Berkeley, the first of his Rancid records. It began as a double album and was cut to one disc.
years.xp: The album was recorded between October 1993 and March 1994. "Salvation" went to alternative radio in early 1995. Wikipedia says it peaked at 97 on the Billboard 200 and went gold in 2000.

years.h: Rancid wins the Bammies' debut prize for Let's Go
years.p: The California Music Awards name it Outstanding Debut Album.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the win among the band's California Music Awards. Rancid took another in 1998 for Life Won't Wait.

years.big: Not the rich label. The punk record guy.
q: We decided it would be dumb not to stay with Brett Gurewitz.
years.h: Madonna's Maverick calls. Rancid stays with Epitaph
years.p: Maverick Records, Madonna's label, was one of several majors that pursued the band. Armstrong turned them all down for Brett Gurewitz.
years.xp:
After Green Day's Dookie and the Offspring's Smash, major labels chased Rancid. Armstrong told the press: "We decided it would be dumb not to stay with Brett Gurewitz." He described Gurewitz as a real punk rock record guy.

Madonna is "an international superstar", he said. Not the fit they needed.

years.h: ...And Out Come the Wolves puts East Bay punk on MTV
years.p: Recorded at Fantasy in Berkeley and Electric Lady in New York, with Gurewitz stepping in when Jerry Finn's schedule fell through.
years.xp:
"Roots Radicals", "Time Bomb" and "Ruby Soho" all charted on Modern Rock Tracks and got heavy MTV rotation. The album peaked at 45 on the Billboard 200, went gold on January 22, 1996, and platinum in 2004. Wikipedia gives August 22 as the release date; the Grammy site says August 15.

"Journey to the End of the East Bay" tells the story of a young band's struggle; "Daly City Train" borrows the BART line.

years.h: Ruby Soho becomes the band's biggest song
years.p: The single reached 13 on Modern Rock Tracks and became a concert staple alongside Time Bomb.

eras.title: Jamaica, Hellcat and the Warner detour
eras.text: Rancid followed the ska and reggae roots, then went back to hardcore, launched Armstrong's own label, and made a strange deal with Warner.

years.h: Armstrong and Gurewitz start Hellcat Records
years.p: Hellcat becomes an Epitaph imprint with Armstrong as talent scout, final say on signings.
years.xp: Armstrong's Wikipedia biography dates Hellcat to 1997; the band's own article says 1999. The first Rancid album on Hellcat was in 2000.

years.h: Life Won't Wait: recorded partly in Kingston
years.p: "Hoover Street" and the title track were cut in Jamaica, with Buju Banton on the title song. Armstrong and Frederiksen produced.
years.xp: Dr. Israel sings on "Coppers", and Dicky Barrett and Billie Joe Armstrong of [[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]] add vocals. Gurewitz only helped with sequencing. It peaked at 35 on the Billboard 200 and 32 in the UK, and won Outstanding Punk/Ska Album at the California Music Awards.

years.h: Rancid (2000): 22 songs in 38 minutes, the first on Hellcat
years.p: Recorded in April 2000 at Westbeach and Sound City, and a hard turn back to hardcore after the ska of Life Won't Wait.
years.xp: Gurewitz returned as producer and stayed for the next five albums. "Let Me Go" was the lone official single, and Armstrong directed a joint video for "Don Giovanni" and "Disgruntled".

years.h: Armstrong forms The Transplants with Rob Aston and Travis Barker
years.p: The side project releases albums in 2002, 2005 and 2017.
years.xp: [[Tim Armstrong|beaecc2d-20c7-4221-8fd2-682c82f0faab]] also produced and wrote for artists from Jimmy Cliff to Pink.

years.h: Indestructible: Warner deal, no Warner logo
years.p: Rancid signed a Warner distribution deal but kept the label's name off the packaging to reassure fans. The album debuted at 15 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
Gurewitz produced across Los Angeles studios; the band cut 25 songs and used 19. A Warner spokesman called it "a unique deal that doesn't play by the traditional record biz rules".

Armstrong's divorce from Brody Dalle informed "Fall Back Down" and "Tropical London". Frederiksen dedicated the closer "Otherside" to his brother Robert, who died in 2001.

eras.title: Side projects and a quiet reunion
eras.text: Everyone scattered: The Transplants, Lars Frederiksen and the Bastards, a stint with Social Distortion. Then the band came back at a Los Angeles club.

years.h: Armstrong, Frederiksen and Freeman go their own ways
years.p: Armstrong tours The Transplants, Frederiksen releases Viking with the Bastards, and Freeman tours with Social Distortion.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Haunted Cities (Transplants, 2005) and Armstrong's solo A Poet's Life (2007) among the projects.

years.h: Hellcat Nights: Rancid plays The Echo again
years.p: The band reforms in early 2006 for a run of shows at the Los Angeles club.

years.h: Founding drummer Brett Reed leaves, [[Branden Steineckert|c6d5c798-dd16-49bf-a085-d9030d85763d]] of The Used takes over
years.p: Reed's last recording had been Indestructible, the only Rancid album with his songwriting.

eras.title: Still standing
eras.text: With Steineckert on drums, Rancid keeps making records, finally tops its own chart mark and tours with Green Day.

years.h: Let the Dominoes Fall: highest chart entry yet
years.p: Booker T. Jones plays organ on "Up to No Good". The album debuted at 11 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: Recorded January 2008 to February 2009 with Gurewitz, it was Steineckert's first album with the band and Rancid's first in six years. European release was June 1, US June 2.

years.h: ...Honor Is All We Know after years of delays
years.p: Work began in 2011 with Gurewitz, and the album peaked at 15 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: A 2012 release slipped, with recording done by March 2013. "Everybody's Sufferin'" covers Laurel Aitken, the band's first cover on a full-length since 1991.

years.h: Trouble Maker debuts at 23
years.p: It sells 18,000 in its first week and hits number 2 on Top Alternative Albums.

years.h: Tomorrow Never Comes: the tenth studio album
years.p: It debuts at 126 on the Billboard 200 but lands in the top 20 on Rock and Alternative Albums.

years.cap: Nova Rock 2017 Tim Armstrong from Rancid at the Nova Rock 2017 · Wikimedia
years.h: Rancid joins Green Day and The Smashing Pumpkins on tour
years.p: The North American Saviors Tour puts the two East Bay bands on the same bill again.
